pairs.subject: rate-limiting
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/management_api.rs:754 writes an api_key_audit DB row (plus an unlatched warn at :749) on every 429, bypassing the limiter once-per-streak latch at src-tauri/engine/src/rate_limiter.rs:78; storm-hygiene budgets the refusal branch as the hot path, so a refusal storm becomes per-request log and SQLite write amplification

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/management_api.rs:754 record_audit(...429...) runs per refusal - a DB insert per rejected request at storm rate; :749 tracing::warn! per refusal duplicates the latched warn
src-tauri/src/engine/management_api.rs:832 rate_limited_response sets the standard Retry-After header from the limiter computed retry_after (body names no rule/window - partial)
src-tauri/src/engine/management_api.rs:745 bucket keyed apikey:{key.id}, a server-assigned id reached only after key lookup and scope check, so callers cannot mint buckets
src-tauri/src/engine/management_api.rs:408 API_KEY_RATE_MAX = 120 carries a rationale (single-user loopback) but no arithmetic and is a compile-time constant, not overridable without a release

pairs.registryProposal: Previous verdict (2026-10-05) cited management_api.rs:739-744; lines drifted to 749/754 - same defect, still live.

pairs.subject: rate-limiting
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/tier_usage.rs:83 infers each bucket limit from its key prefix (webhook: else event_source_max), so apikey: (enforced 120, management_api.rs:408), tool: and mcp_tool: (enforced 30, rate_limiter.rs:175) buckets are charted against the wrong limit and feed approaching_limit at :109; limit-observability requires one arithmetic for operator and caller

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/tier_usage.rs:83 limit guessed from key spelling because the limiter owns no policy (check() takes max/window per call, src-tauri/engine/src/rate_limiter.rs:50) - the exact failure the golden path names
src-tauri/src/commands/infrastructure/tier_usage.rs:109 approaching_limit computed from the mis-derived percent, so the near-limit warning is false for every non-webhook non-event key family

pairs.registryProposal: The root cause sits in rate_limiter.rs (policy as call-site parameter), which context-map files under test-runner-lab (6a81750d-fdbf-4518-bae6-689303e1a884) - a context with no rate-limiting pair. Missing pairing: test-runner-lab x rate-limiting, or the file belongs in an engine context.

pairs.subject: rate-limiting
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs:409 refuses with 429 and no_headers() (retry-after only in body prose); refusal-contract requires the protocol standard Retry-After header, which the same file already sets on its 422 path at webhook.rs:499 - header-honouring senders get nothing and guess

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs:409 no_headers() on the 429 path while :499 inserts retry-after on the 422 active-hours path

src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs:402 tracing::warn! on every refused webhook, defeating the limiter latch at src-tauri/engine/src/rate_limiter.rs:78 (tool_runner.rs and mcp_tools.rs refusal branches do the same)
src-tauri/src/engine/webhook.rs:396 key webhook:{trigger_id} is formed only after trigger_repo::get_by_id at :350 rejects unknown ids, so a caller cannot mint a fresh bucket per request
src-tauri/src/engine/mcp_tools.rs:793 keys mcp_tool:{credential_id}:{tool_name} on the server-assigned credential so caller-chosen gateway prefixes cannot split one tool into many allowances
